name: Strengths Finder Test
tagline: Discover your natural talents and where they shine at work.
intro: Everyone has natural talents: ways of thinking, feeling and acting that come easily and give energy. This test maps your talents across four domains: getting things done, influencing others, building relationships and thinking. Rate 100 short statements on how well they fit you. In about five minutes you learn your strongest domain, the roles that suit you and how to use your talents more.
seoTitle: Strengths Finder Test – Find your natural talents
seoDescription: Discover your strongest talent domain in 5 minutes: getting things done, influencing, relating or thinking. Free test with ideal roles and practical tips.

executing.name: Getting Things Done
executing.short: Your talent for turning plans into finished, reliable results.
executing.low: Getting things done is not where your natural talent lies. Planning, detail work and steady follow-through may cost you more energy than they give. That is fine: your strengths are probably elsewhere. Rather than forcing yourself into roles built on routine execution, team up with someone who loves structure and deadlines. Use simple tools, such as a short daily to-do list or calendar reminders, to cover the basics without draining yourself.
executing.mid: You have a reliable capacity for getting things done. You can plan, follow through and meet deadlines, especially when the goal matters to you, but execution is not always what energises you most. You can handle roles with a mix of doing and thinking or connecting. Strengthen this domain by choosing one system for tasks and sticking to it, and by setting clear finish lines so projects do not drift.
executing.high: Getting things done is your strongest talent domain. You turn ideas into results, love progress and are someone others can count on. You thrive in roles such as project manager, operations lead, coordinator, engineer, event planner or any job with clear goals and visible output. Use this talent by owning deliverables, building processes others can follow and helping your team stay on track. Watch out for overload: say no to tasks that do not serve your priorities.

influencing.name: Persuading & Mobilising
influencing.short: Your talent for convincing, inspiring and moving people to act.
influencing.low: Influencing others is not your most natural talent. Selling ideas, taking the floor or competing may feel uncomfortable or tiring. That is no problem: many strong contributors work best behind the scenes. When your ideas need support, partner with a natural persuader, or let solid evidence and quality speak for you. If you want to grow here, practise presenting in a small, safe group first and prepare two or three key points.
influencing.mid: You have a reasonable talent for influencing. You can speak up, persuade and take charge when needed, though you may not seek the spotlight. This flexibility helps in roles that combine influence with expertise, such as specialist adviser or team lead. To build on it, practise framing your ideas around what your audience cares about, and take on one visible task, such as presenting results, to grow your confidence.
influencing.high: Influencing is your strongest talent domain. You persuade, energise and mobilise people, and you are comfortable taking charge and speaking up. You thrive in roles such as sales, business development, entrepreneurship, leadership, advocacy, politics or public speaking. Use this talent by championing ideas you believe in, representing your team and opening doors for others. Make sure you also listen carefully, so people feel heard rather than pushed, and choose your battles wisely.

relating.name: Connecting & Bonding
relating.short: Your talent for building trust, teams and lasting relationships.
relating.low: Building relationships is not your most natural talent area. You may prefer to focus on tasks, ideas or results rather than on people's feelings and team dynamics. That focus can be very productive. Still, trust makes everything easier. Try simple habits: ask colleagues one personal question a week or thank someone specifically for their help. In team roles, work closely with someone who naturally looks after the group's mood.
relating.mid: You have a solid talent for relating to people. You can build trust and support others while also keeping your focus on the work. This makes you a valued team member in almost any role. To strengthen this domain, invest a little time in one-to-one conversations and notice who might need encouragement. Asking good questions and remembering what people tell you are easy ways to deepen your working relationships.
relating.high: Building relationships is your strongest talent domain. You create trust, read people well and help groups work together in harmony. You thrive in roles such as team leader, coach, HR or people manager, teacher, account manager, nurse, counsellor or community builder. Use this talent by mentoring colleagues, bridging conflicts and welcoming newcomers. Protect your energy by not taking on everyone's problems, and remember that honest feedback is also an act of care.

thinking.name: Analysing & Imagining
thinking.short: Your talent for analysing, learning and seeing future possibilities.
thinking.low: Analytical and strategic thinking are not your most natural talents. You probably prefer action, people or practical results over long reflection and abstract ideas. That makes you quick and grounded. To avoid blind spots, involve a thoughtful colleague before big decisions, and use simple tools such as a pros-and-cons list. You do not need to become a strategist; you only need to make sure the thinking gets done by someone.
thinking.mid: You have a sound talent for thinking. You can analyse problems, learn quickly and consider the future, while staying practical. This makes you a useful bridge between planners and doers. Strengthen this domain by blocking regular time to reflect on your work and by asking what could happen next before acting. Reading or listening to one thought-provoking source a week also keeps your thinking sharp.
thinking.high: Thinking is your strongest talent domain. You analyse, learn, connect ideas and imagine future possibilities with ease. You thrive in roles such as strategist, analyst, researcher, consultant, data scientist, architect, policy adviser or product designer. Use this talent by tackling complex problems, shaping long-term plans and helping others see the bigger picture. Share your thinking in clear, simple steps, and set deadlines so analysis turns into action rather than endless reflection.

summary: Your talents fall into four broad domains. Below you see how strongly each one shows up in your answers, with your strongest domain highlighted as your main talent area. Focus on developing your top domain; for lower domains, it is often smarter to partner with people who are strong there than to force yourself.
